entry.evidence: However, crust–mantle evolution and crustal response to the Indian lithospheric subduction are still controversial.

sequences.source_document: Published paper (PDF body text, XML abstract and captions)

steps.action: The authors pose the question of how the crust beneath the Qiangtang and Songpan-Ganzi terranes responds to Indian subduction, and say that answering it needs more information on crustal structure.
steps.quote: Answering these questions requires additional information regarding crustal structure.

steps.action: The authors take rival models from the literature: the subduction-front position (Bangong-Nujiang suture, central Qiangtang, or north Qiangtang), lateral extrusion, and lower crustal flow.
steps.quote: the penetration distance of the subduction front is still debated

steps.action: The authors take ground-based gravity and elevation data from 224 sites on the Riwoqe-Yushu-Mado profile, collected by the Institute of Seismology and published earlier with the authors as co-authors [23], and tie them to the absolute gravity benchmark at Yushu.
steps.quote: The dataset of 224 measurement sites was consisted of gravity readings

steps.action: The authors apply normal-gravity, Bouguer and terrain corrections to obtain the complete Bouguer gravity anomaly, and describe its five fault-bounded segments and their linear trends (Fig. 2).
steps.quote: After the corrections of normal gravity, Bouguer and terrain, the complete BGA was obtained

steps.action: The authors take the 2-D NFG method from prior work: a Fourier sine-series representation with downward analytical continuation, normalized by the mean full gradient.
steps.quote: It minimizes the high-frequency noise of the observed gravity data

steps.action: The authors design a new synthetic model with two prisms at the same horizontal position but different depths and scales, and run NFG on the combined model (N = 63, 315) and on each prism alone (N = 125, 280) to test whether multi-scale sources can be located.
steps.quote: was designed to test the efficiency of multi-scale anomalous source determination

steps.action: From the synthetic test, the authors conclude that field applications need several optimum harmonic numbers rather than one.
steps.quote: We concluded that the complex crustal structure is not bounded by one optimum harmonic number (OHN) in field applications

steps.action: The authors set the processing: 2 km interpolation and continuation interval, removal of a second-order polynomial regional trend, and selection of the harmonic numbers 33, 43, 53 and 71 from the NFGMax curve and the energy ratio Er (Fig. 4).
steps.quote: we used 33, 43, 53 and 71 as the OHNs for interpretation of the multi-scale wavelength

steps.action: The authors compute the NFG section for N = 33 and identify three long-wavelength anomalous sources, including a northeastward-dipping anomaly between the Bangong-Nujiang suture and the Zhanaqu fault (F3).
steps.quote: three regions with relatively high NFGs appeared in this section

steps.action: The authors compare the N = 33 anomalies with published post-collisional magmatism, lithospheric downwelling, and deep seismic sounding crustal boundaries.
steps.quote: This is consistent with lithospheric downwelling near the Bangong-Nujiang suture

steps.action: The authors compute the NFG sections for N = 43 and N = 53, and locate a large lower-crust to uppermost-mantle source beneath the Jinsha suture plus the splitting of shallower anomalies.
steps.quote: The most distinct anomalous sources inferred from the two NFG images were located in the lower crust and uppermost mantle

steps.action: The authors compare the Jinsha source with Moho downwelling from deep seismic sounding, low resistivity and low-velocity bodies, and name two rival origins: lower crustal flow or underplating.
steps.quote: which may result from lower crustal flow [11,34] or underplating beneath the Jinsha suture [4]

steps.action: The authors compute the NFG section for N = 71, discount a lower-crust anomaly near 50 km as a boundary effect, and locate an upper-crust source about 10 km deep beneath the Ganzi-Yushu fault.
steps.quote: The NFGMax was located at a depth of approximately 10 km

steps.action: The authors compare the N = 71 source with the USGS hypocenter of the 2010 Yushu earthquake and with a published high-velocity upper-crust anomaly.
steps.quote: The focus of the 2010 MW6.9 Yushu earthquake was located near the relative NFGMax

steps.action: Using the synthetic horizontal-prism pattern, the authors offer an alternative reading of the high NFG beneath the Deqin fault as a horizontal upper-crust source.
steps.quote: An alternative interpretation with the relatively high NFG beneath the Deqin fault (F4) is similar to the

steps.action: The authors set the dipping anomaly against subduction models: it is taken to support Indian mantle penetration to southern or central Qiangtang, but not the shallow-angle model.
steps.quote: Our results support the possible scenario that the Indian lithospheric mantle penetrates as far as the southern or central Qiangtang terrane

steps.action: The authors adopt from the literature the conditional scenario that the lower crustal flow direction changed from northward to eastward.
steps.quote: A possible scenario is that the flow direction of the lower crust changed from northward to eastward

steps.action: Under that scenario, the authors read the Jinsha lower-crust source as an obstacle to the flow and the Ganzi-Yushu fault as the flow channel's north margin, supported by published effective elastic thickness and velocity results.
steps.quote: our NFG results suggest that the Ganzi-Yushu fault (F6) can be considered the north margin of the crustal channel flow

steps.action: The authors keep the N = 71 upper-crust source as the probable seismogenic body of the 2010 Yushu event, citing its coincidence with a published low-velocity body.
steps.quote: may be inferred as the seismogenic body of the 2010 Yushu event

steps.action: The authors combine the subduction-related, flow-related and earthquake-related structures into one schematic cross-section of the crust.
steps.quote: Diagrammatic cross-section of the crustal structure in the Qiangtang and the Songpan-Ganzi terranes, eastern Tibet.

steps.action: The authors conclude with three qualitative crustal structures and their tectonic interpretations.
steps.quote: Our results, although not quantitative, provided useful information on three crustal structures.

end.claim: NFG sections of the Bouguer anomaly show a northeastward-dipping source beneath southern Qiangtang, read as Indian underthrusting; a large lower-crust source beneath the Jinsha suture, read as thickening crust resisting lower crustal flow; and an upper-crust source beneath the Ganzi-Yushu fault, read as the 2010 Yushu seismogenic body.

decisive_move.sentence: Without the multi-harmonic NFG sections (N = 33, 43, 53, 71) computed from the Bouguer profile, none of the three anomalous sources, and so none of the tectonic claims, would exist.

gates.evidence: Action: the gravity data are an inherited profile dataset [23]; no stated hypothesis directed their acquisition. Claim: only the method faced a test it could have failed, the synthetic two-prism model (pp. 537-539). The tectonic interpretations are checked only for consistency with published studies (pp. 539-541). Registration: the harmonic numbers were picked after inspecting the NFGMax and Er curves (p. 539), and in the synthetic test N = 63 was accepted 'after testing a large quantity of harmonic numbers' (p. 537).

imports.item: Finite Fourier sine series and analytic downward continuation as the basis of the NFG operator
Cubic interpolation of the profile to a 2 km grid

novelty_claims.quote: there is an absence of a combined model reconstructing anomalous sources at the same horizontal locations and significantly different scales and depths
a new model composed of two horizontal infinity prisms
Our results distinguished the seismogenic body from the crustal transitional zone

limits:
Coding sources: the XML text has only the abstract and captions, so body quotes and locations come from the PDF text, and some quotes avoid PDF extraction artifacts. No review file was supplied, so there is no review sequence.

Data: the gravity data were collected in earlier work involving the authors [23]. Whether the corrections were redone here is not stated (inference).

What the paper does not show:
- No uncertainty or resolution is given for source depths or extents.
- No sensitivity test of the field results to the regional polynomial order, the interpolation interval, or the OHN choice.
- No density forward modelling is used to test the interpreted sources.
- The boundary-effect anomaly near 50 km is dismissed without a test.
- Comparisons with deep seismic sounding, velocity and resistivity studies are qualitative.
- Rivals (flow vs underplating; subduction-front positions) are named but no prediction separates them.
- Fault labelling is inconsistent: the text calls F4 the Deqin fault while the Fig. 2 caption calls it the Zigasi fault.

Sub-claims at other statuses:
- The NFG multi-OHN method on synthetic prisms: capability_characterized.
- The seismogenic-body reading is hedged ('may be inferred') and weaker than best_explanation.
- The Indian penetration claim is stated as support for a 'possible scenario'.

Composition is none_fits because the walk applies an existing method (with a synthetic check) to one inherited profile, then interprets by consistency with literature. Conditions are found, but there is no series of independent traces and no rival test, so trace_series does not quite fit (inference).

disagreements.target: Shallow-angle subduction model beneath eastern Qiangtang (Agius & Lebedev 2013 [9])
disagreements.support: The NFG sections show a dipping source only beneath southern Qiangtang and no dipping structures farther north, which the authors read as not supporting shallow-angle subduction.
disagreements.quote: [...] cannot confirm the shallow-angle subduction model underneath the eastern Qiangtang terrane [9]
